mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a true fruit?

options.A: It develops solely from the ovary of the flower.
options.B: It develops from the receptacle surrounding the ovary.
options.C: It is always a fleshy type of fruit.
options.D: It is formed from the inflorescence rather than a single flower.

mcqs.answer: It develops solely from the ovary of the flower.
mcqs.explanation: A true fruit is derived only from the mature ovary of a single flower. Options B, C, and D describe false fruits or are inaccurate statements.

mcqs.question: A simple fruit develops from a single, syncarpous ovary that is fleshy. Which type of simple fruit does this description best fit?
mcqs.explanation: Berries arise from a single ovary that is fleshy throughout, such as grapes or tomatoes. Drupes have a hard endocarp, pomes are accessory fruits, and samaras are winged achenes, none of which match the given description.

mcqs.question: Which characteristic distinguishes an aggregate fruit from a multiple fruit?

options.A: It is formed from many ovaries of a single flower.
options.B: It is formed from ovaries of several different flowers.
options.C: It develops exclusively from the receptacle tissue.
options.D: It is always a dry, dehiscent fruit.

mcqs.answer: It is formed from many ovaries of a single flower.
mcqs.explanation: Aggregate fruits (e.g., raspberry) arise when each carpel of one flower develops into a small fruit that remains attached. Multiple fruits (e.g., pineapple) develop from the ovaries of many flowers. Options C and D are unrelated to the distinction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a classic example of a multiple fruit?
mcqs.explanation: Pineapple is formed from the fusion of ovaries of many individual flowers in an inflorescence, making it a multiple fruit. Strawberry is an accessory (false) fruit, raspberry is an aggregate fruit, and fig is a syconium (a type of multiple fruit but not the standard example used in NCERT; pineapple is the textbook example).

mcqs.question: In botanical terminology, a fruit is best defined as:

options.A: The mature ovary of a flower, often containing seeds.
options.B: Any edible part of a plant that is sweet and fleshy.
options.C: The part of the plant that produces pollen.
options.D: A modified leaf that protects the seed.

mcqs.answer: The mature ovary of a flower, often containing seeds.
mcqs.explanation: Botanically, a fruit is the mature ovary after fertilisation, usually enclosing seeds. Options B, C, and D describe other plant structures or are too broad.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a false (accessory) fruit?
mcqs.explanation: In a strawberry, the fleshy part is derived from the receptacle (the flower base), while the actual fruits are the tiny achenes on its surface, making it a false or accessory fruit. Apples, peaches, and cherries develop from the ovary itself, thus are true fruits.

mcqs.question: Which definition correctly distinguishes a simple fruit from an aggregate fruit?

options.A: A simple fruit develops from a single ovary of one flower; an aggregate fruit develops from multiple ovaries of the same flower.
options.B: A simple fruit develops from many flowers; an aggregate fruit develops from a single flower.
options.C: A simple fruit is always dry; an aggregate fruit is always fleshy.
options.D: A simple fruit is formed from the receptacle; an aggregate fruit is formed from the ovary.

mcqs.answer: A simple fruit develops from a single ovary of one flower; an aggregate fruit develops from multiple ovaries of the same flower.
mcqs.explanation: Simple fruits arise from one ovary of a single flower (e.g., mango), whereas aggregate fruits arise when several carpels of one flower each develop into small fruits that stay together (e.g., raspberry). The other options mix up the definitions.

mcqs.question: A plant produces many small, fleshy units each derived from separate carpels of a single flower that remain attached. What type of fruit is this?
mcqs.explanation: When each carpel of one flower forms an individual fruitlet that stays together, the result is an aggregate fruit (e.g., blackberry). Simple fruits come from one ovary, multiple fruits from many flowers, and accessory fruits involve non‑ovarian tissue.
